the_grammar_these_seal: The renderings fix the grammar before the renderer exists, which is the
point of sealing them. In words:
1. R(s) is read left to right as a token stream: the longest matching row of
the committed lexicon, else a numeric literal, else an identifier.
2. Every lexicon token emits its phrase. Every numeric literal emits the
registered numeral pair's words. Every identifier that is not a type name
emits `variable ` followed by the numeral words of its slot index, where
indices are assigned by FIRST OCCURRENCE in R(s), left to right, from
zero.
3. Emissions are joined by single spaces. Nothing else is emitted.
PRECEDENCE IS CARRIED, NOT REBUILT: R(s)'s own parentheses become `the
quantity` / `end quantity` and no bracket is added, because the inverse
feeds the result back to the same grammar it came from. This is narrower
than v0.18's realizer, which had to re-bracket for a different grammar.
IDENTIFIERS ARE ERASED TO INDICES on purpose: Serialize.lean drops the Name
field of every binder, so a rendered name would be information the identity
witness cannot see — a rendering error B1 could never catch.
NUMERALS ARE UNSIGNED: `-` is always the operator row, so the numeral pair's
word `negative` never appears and there is exactly one `-` row.
A parenthesised binder group renders its parentheses like any other, so
`∃ (x y z : Rat),` reads `for some the quantity variable zero variable one
variable two of type rational end quantity it holds that` — awkward, and
correct, and sealed rather than tidied.
what_this_is: One hundred hand-authored renderings, committed VERBATIM as a SEALED
PREDICTION. DESIGN-foreign-voice's adversarial review required the
three-line separation this file is the third line of: the lexicon digest is
frozen before these exist; the ids follow from that digest by a committed
rule; and these renderings are what scripts/foreign_voice.py must later
reproduce BYTE-IDENTICALLY. Every divergence is REPORTED in the run
artifact, never repaired. 'A hand probe whose outputs are never compared
against the implementation is a rehearsal, not a gate.'
They are authored against R(s), not against the corpus source, because with
autoImplicit off the surface must carry an explicit binder preamble and the
sentence a reader sees is the sentence for the statement UNDER THE DECLARED
